source: derived from the clause 4.3 administrative record layout
note: Bundle Protocol wire layer, narrowly scoped. Most of BP's encoding is built from SDNVs, pinned independently and more thoroughly in vectors/sdnv/sdnv.json; duplicating them here would add no coverage and a second place to drift. Endpoint identifiers are URI strings rather than octet fields. What is left and worth pinning is the administrative record's type and flags octet, where the two share one octet. There are no decode vectors: a full record needs a body whose layout depends on the record type, which is beyond what this file scopes. Bundle reassembly, fragmentation and custody transfer are not covered.

encode.name: admin-record-status-report-type-octet
encode.note: The administrative record opens with one octet: the record type in the high nibble, flags in the low nibble. A status report with no flags is type 1<<4 = 0x10.

encode.name: admin-record-custody-signal-type-octet
encode.note: A custody signal is type 2: 2<<4 = 0x20. Paired with the status report vector, this pins that the type occupies the high nibble and not the low one.

encode.name: admin-record-fragment-flag
encode.note: A status report for a fragment sets the fragment flag in the low nibble: 1<<4 | 1 = 0x11. Type and flags share the octet, so a decoder reading the whole octet as a type fails here.

reject.name: admin-record-type-not-defined
reject.note: Record type 0xf (from octet 0xf0) is not a defined administrative record type. A decoder must refuse rather than process the body under an unknown record layout.

reject.name: admin-record-empty
reject.note: No octets at all: not even the type and flags octet is present.
